To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the induction of neutralising antibodies to a chronic viral infection can be improved by reducing the T-cell help that normally promotes the production of non-neutralising antibodies.
polyclonal activation of B cells impairs neutralizing antibody production and that the deliberate reduction of T cell help can be used to induce potent neutralizing antibody production.
polyclonal B-cell activation in vivo impairs the induction neutralizing antibody responses.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development and application of novel strategies to induce protective antibody responses against viruses.
the mechanisms underlying antibody responses to viruses.
the mechanisms of the B cell response to virus infection and the development of novel strategies to improve the induction of neutralising antibodies.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
T cell help is required to induce neutralizing antibody responses, but that this T cell help may be detrimental in the case of polyclonal activation of B cells.
the removal of CD4+ T cells from the host, as a result of the HIV-1 infection, is not a cause for the development of neutralizing antibodies.
the induction of virus-specific T cell responses can be improved by deliberate removal of CD4+ T cells.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the induction of a polyclonal B-cell response can impair the induction of neutralising antibody production.
, in contrast to the common belief, T cell help can sometimes be detrimental.
polyclonal B cells activation can be a double-edged sword.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the B cell response to infection can be divided into two distinct phases.

polyclonal B-cell activation, which is a hallmark of the immune response to viruses, can impair virus-specific antibody responses, and thus, that CD4+ T-cell help is not always beneficial for the production of neutralizing antibodies.
polyclonal B-cell activation may be an obstacle to the generation of neutralizing antibody titers in vivo.
